claim: Missed shared subject: the per-family facts of the underground's marks. V04 §5.2 gives the `rock` role only for `ink`, `lit` and `hatched` ("item 413: `ink` a 40 %-ink cross-hatch at 1.2 paper px; `lit` a dark stone fill; `hatched` its dense hatch", V04 l. 2713–2714) and says nothing of `void` or the `under.*` semantics in `parchment`, `bw-print`, `night` or `painterly`, while §8.2 ships all seven (l. 12772–12773) and refuses a sheet with an unresolved (semantic, pass) pair (l. 12748). The village product opens in `painterly` (V07 §5.1) and draws the underground at village rungs (V04 §3.1: "The village product shows the layer"; V07 §3.16), and V07 §5.1 leaves the underground's marks to "V04's programs" (V07 l. 3243–3245), so no member defines `painterly`'s rock, void or `under.*` rows. V05 §5.1 is the precedent: the layer's volume states every shipped sheet's facts and that every shipped sheet resolves its semantics.
required_change: V04 §5.2 adds the per-family facts of `rock`, `void` and each `under.*` semantic for every shipped sheet of §8.2's presets table — `ink`, `lit`, `hatched`, the ink-family variants `parchment`, `bw-print` (on its grey ramp) and `night`, and `painterly` from V07's V-M1 (in V07 §5.1's palette, agreed with V07) — and the sentence "every shipped sheet resolves every `under.*` semantic, so the loader never refuses one; a user sheet missing one resolves it by §8.2's slot resolution", with T-V4's render bar (the one that loads the layer at every band) loading every shipped sheet; §8.2 cites it (VAL-R1-05).

claim: Partly fixed. V06 now keys the dig draw as V04 does and draws again for each wing V02's mutator adds over a void. This is V06 §3.18.1 (2a), l.2461-2467: 'A building draws once per void kind, plus once for each wing V02's mutator adds over a void (a `MutationPlan` step or a rung-3 op, in `scope.basementGrown`)'. T-V6-34 and bar.T-V6-34 read 'one draw per (lineage, void kind, added-wing key)'. V04 §3.5.7 (d), the rule's home, still ends: 'and a building never draws twice for one kind' (l.1855-1857). That clause was there in round 0 too. So the home now contradicts its own key clause ('its key carrying the wing key of a wing V02's mutator adds', l.1846) and V06. A build that follows V04's last clause makes no second draw for an added wing and fails T-V6-34.
required_change: In V04 §3.5.7 (d) replace 'and a building never draws twice for one kind.' with 'and a building draws once per void kind, plus once for each wing V02's mutator adds over a void (a `MutationPlan` step or a rung-3 op), its key carrying that wing's key, never twice for one key (V06 §3.18.1 (2a); T-V6-34).' Keep the rest of (d), with 'Item 109 (d)'s "chance raised over a ruin" is this row.' after it.

V04 §5.1 *Find on Below* (4) (l.2692-2696, added this round): 'Show gaps' units Below are the undercity districts, each outlined dashed "none here" in the band holding its core'. V01 §5.4 (1) and (3) list as Below's `district` units 'each undercity neighbourhood and the underground pseudo-district' (V04 §3.6a (5)), and the per-plot `walk` and `households` units read `underDistance` there. V04 §3.6a (5) itself makes 'each undercity neighbourhood and the underground pseudo-district (the sewer-front neighbourhoods and F6's void dwellings) … a catchment of its own'. So under V04 a sewer-front neighbourhood or a void-dwelling cluster without the chip's class is never outlined, and a walk-counted class Below is read by district.
required_change: In V04 §5.1 *Find on Below* (4) replace 'Show gaps' units Below are the undercity districts, each outlined dashed "none here" in the band holding its core.' with 'Show gaps' units Below are V01 §5.4 (3)'s `gapUnits` on the underground parts, restating none. Each undercity neighbourhood and the underground pseudo-district is a `district` unit (V04 §3.6a (5)), and the per-plot units read `underDistance`. Each gap is outlined dashed "none here" in every band holding its plots, an undercity neighbourhood's in the band holding its core.' Make UE32 and T-V4-81 name the pseudo-district's gap.

claim: V04 §3.2 N7 (1) and N2 do not read the moat level §4.2 S3 (10) now derives. N7 says 'the terrain's height at the shore stands for the water surface, as §2.6's water table reads it, so the mouth sits `outfall.freeboardCm` above the water it discharges into'. The base, after its VEW-04 repair, says the moat's water level is one derived value — the `flowFrom` source's shore height — 'which every reader of the moat's water reads (… V04 §3.2 N2 and N7 …)', and the moat's banks stand up to `moat.maxFallCm` (400 cm) above it. On a moat outfall (N2's per-bank fallback) N7 therefore puts the mouth's floor up to 4 m above the moat's water, and the 'mouth sits `freeboardCm` above the water' rule (T-V4-2's 'every outfall invert ≥ the shore height + `freeboardCm`') is checked against the bank, not the water.
required_change: V04 §3.2 N7 (1): 'Each outfall knot's floor is `low = s + freeboardCm`, `s` the receiving water's surface as §2.6's water table reads it — a moat's the derived level of §4.2 S3 (10), every other body's terrain height at the shore'. T-V4-2's outfall clause reads the same `s`; T-V4-80 (j)'s walled-core-in-a-wet-moat fixture adds a moat on sloping ground.

claim: VEW-01's new rule makes N2's moat and field fallbacks 'taken per bank (N3: the parts of the graph the water divides …)', but N3 builds that graph after N2 and includes 'N2's outfall-run edges' in it; the text neither orders the steps (banks before N2's per-bank admission and fallbacks, outfall runs after), nor says which bank an outfall candidate belongs to, nor how 'the bank's stretch of `R`'s boundary' (the field outfall's search and the no-dry-boundary case) is cut from `R`'s boundary when banks are graph components rather than land regions. Two implementations could choose different outfalls for the same seed (ambiguous normative text in a deterministic stage).
required_change: In V04 §3.2 state: (a) the order — N3's way, culvert and drainage edges first (without N2's outfall runs), then the banks (their components with the stretches over water left out), then N2's admission per bank and its moat and field fallbacks, then the outfall-run edges joining the graph; (b) a candidate's bank — the bank of the way junction its outfall run links (a candidate linking none dropped, as now); (c) a bank's stretch of `R`'s boundary by a stated rule (e.g. the boundary `hydro` cells whose nearest graph node, by distance then address, lies on that bank), so the field outfall and the gutter-and-pit case read one partition; T-V4-80 (j) unchanged.
